sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Thousands of 15th-century stained glass fragments from Coventry cathedral have been catalogued and photographed. Packed into 30 wooden crates following 1940 Luftwaffe bombing, the remnants survived both the Reformation and the second world war. Led by stained glass conservator Laura Atkinson, the project offers virtual public access to the collection.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Experts consider the glass, attributed to master glazier John Thornton, to be an internationally significant treasure trove. The fragments depict biblical scenes, donors, animals and intricate jewels, showcasing high-end medieval craftsmanship. Digital access allows researchers to study glassmaking techniques, track medieval craftspeople, and potentially use AI to reconstruct original window designs.

sections.heading: What happens next

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Private BitTorrent trackers operate as exclusive, invite-only communities where users share and curate vast catalogues of pirated media. Members adhere to strict community rules, maintaining upload-to-download ratios by seeding content to gain rank and access to more exclusive servers. Some users actively seek out long-lost or rare media, such as unpublished literary works and obscure documentaries, to upload and preserve them.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Supporters and researchers argue that private trackers act as digital archives preserving cultural material absent from commercial streaming platforms. However, copyright enforcement bodies like the Motion Picture Association view private trackers as illegal operations that feed broader unauthorized distribution networks.

sections.heading: What happens next
